```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

out_dir <- "../results/downstream_plots"
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

library(SNPRelate)
library(gdsfmt)
library(vcfR)
library(triangulaR)
library(pophelper)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)
library(reshape2)
```


## 1. Data Initialization
We are now linking your previous 3-loci genotypes (*G, T, F1, O*) with the high-resolution SNP data to see where they conflict or align.

```{r data_paths}
master_vcf_path <- "../results/filtered_vcf/merged_final.vcf.gz"
metadata_path   <- "../raw/popMap_Loc_geno.txt" # The file you just provided

# Load Metadata
metadata <- read.delim(metadata_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
# Clean sample names to ensure matching with VCF
metadata$Sample <- trimws(metadata$Sample)

# Stats Files Paths (for Diversity/Fst sections)
pi_path         <- "../results/pixy/merged_pi_pi.txt"
het_path        <- "../results/filtered_vcf/heterozygous_merged.het"
fst_spec_path   <- "../results/populations/merged_final.p.fst_summary.tsv"

# Create a population map for triangulaR (Defining 'pure' reference groups)
# We use your 'G' and 'T' designations as the reference parents
hybrid_popmap <- metadata %>% 
  filter(Genotype %in% c("G", "T")) %>%
  select(id = Sample, pop = Genotype)

```


## Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
PCA provides a broad view of how individuals cluster. We expect G and T to form distinct clusters, with hybrids positioned between them.

```{r}
gds_file <- "mytilus_data.gds"
if (!file.exists(gds_file)) {
  snpgdsVCF2GDS(master_vcf_path, gds_file, method="biallelic.only")
}

showfile.gds(closeall=TRUE, verbose=FALSE)
genofile <- snpgdsOpen(gds_file)
pca_results <- snpgdsPCA(genofile, autosome.only=FALSE)

# Calculate variance explained
pc_var <- pca_results$varprop * 100

# Format PCA dataframe
pca_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = pca_results$sample.id,
  PC1 = pca_results$eigenvect[,1],
  PC2 = pca_results$eigenvect[,2]
) %>% left_join(metadata, by = "Sample")

# Plot PCA colored by previous Genotype and shaped by Location
p_pca <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(x=PC1, y=PC2, color=Genotype, shape=Location)) +
  geom_point(size=4, alpha=0.8) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("G"="#377eb8", "T"="#e41a1c", "F1"="#4daf4a", "O"="#984ea3")) +
  labs(title="PCA: SNP-based Clustering of Mytilus",
       x=paste0("PC1 (", round(pc_var[1], 2), "%)"),
       y=paste0("PC2 (", round(pc_var[2], 2), "%)"))
p_pca
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "PCA_plot.png"), p_pca, width=8, height=6, dpi=300)

write.csv(pca_df, file.path(out_dir, "PCA_data.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
snpgdsClose(genofile)

```



## 3. Genomic Ancestry by Collection Site
Instead of just a PCA, we want to see the specific "mixture" of alleles for every individual, organized by where they were collected.

```{r structure_by_site, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
# Assuming you have run ADMIXTURE or Structure
struct_path <- "../results/admixture/"
struct_files <- list.files(path = struct_path, pattern = ".*.2.meanQ$", full.names=TRUE) # K=2 for G vs T

if(length(struct_files) > 0) {
  # Load ancestry coefficients
  slist <- readQ(files=struct_files)
  
  # Read sample order from .fam file
  fam <- read.table("../results/admixture/Mytilus_structure.fam", header=FALSE)
  rownames(slist[[1]]) <- fam$V2
  
  q_df <- as.data.frame(slist[[1]])
  q_df$Sample <- rownames(q_df)
  
  # Join with your metadata to get Location and previous Genotype
  viz_df <- left_join(q_df, metadata, by = "Sample")
  
  # Melt for ggplot
  viz_long <- melt(viz_df, id.vars = c("Sample", "Location", "Genotype"))

  # Plot barplot grouped by Collection Site
  p_ancestry <- ggplot(viz_long, aes(x = Sample, y = value, fill = variable)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
    facet_grid(~Location, scales = "free_x", space = "free") +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("G" = "#377eb8", "T" = "#e41a1c"), 
                      labels = c("M. galloprovincialis", "M. trossulus")) +
    labs(title = "Individual Ancestry Proportions by Collection Site",
         y = "Ancestry Proportion", x = "Individual") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
  p_ancestry

  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Ancestry_by_site.png"), p_ancestry, width=12, height=5, dpi=300)}
  write.csv(viz_df, file.path(out_dir, "Ancestry_data.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

## 4. SNP-Based Hybrid Index vs. Heterozygosity
This is the "Triangle Plot" logic. It tells you if an individual is a true F1 (high hybrid index ~0.5 AND high heterozygosity) or a backcross (high index but lower heterozygosity).

```{r triangle_analysis}
vcf_data <- read.vcfR(master_vcf_path, verbose = FALSE)

# Subset VCF to only samples in hybrid_popmap (pure G and T references)
vcf_samples <- colnames(vcf_data@gt)[-1]
common_samples <- intersect(vcf_samples, hybrid_popmap$id)
hybrid_popmap <- hybrid_popmap %>% filter(id %in% common_samples)
vcf_hybrid <- vcf_data[, c("FORMAT", common_samples)]

# Identify diagnostic markers based on your 'G' and 'T' references
diff_markers <- alleleFreqDiff(vcfR = vcf_hybrid, pm = hybrid_popmap, 
                               p1 = "G", p2 = "T", difference = 0.8)

# Calculate Hybrid Index (S) and Heterozygosity (H)
hi_results <- hybridIndex(vcfR = diff_markers, pm = hybrid_popmap, p1 = "G", p2 = "T")

# Merge with your original 3-loci designations to see how they hold up
comparison_df <- left_join(hi_results, metadata, by = c("id" = "Sample"))

p_triangle <- ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = hybrid.index, y = heterozygosity, color = Genotype)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = 0.5, yend = 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0.5, y = 1, xend = 1, yend = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "SNP Hybrid Index vs Heterozygosity",
       subtitle = "Colors represent original 3-loci designations",
       x = "Hybrid Index (0=G, 1=T)", y = "Interclass Heterozygosity")

p_triangle
write.csv(comparison_df, file.path(out_dir, "Hybrid_index_data.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Triangle_plot.png"), p_triangle, width=8, height=6, dpi=300)
```

## 5. Summary Statistics by Site
```{r site_summary}
site_summary <- comparison_df %>%
  group_by(Location) %>%
  summarize(
    N = n(),
    Mean_H_Index = mean(hybrid.index, na.rm=TRUE),
    Prop_Hybrids = sum(hybrid.index > 0.1 & hybrid.index < 0.9) / n()
  )

knitr::kable(site_summary, caption = "Hybridization Summary by Collection Site")
write.csv(site_summary, file.path(out_dir, "Site_summary.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

## 6. Optimal K Selection & Multi-K Ancestry Barplots
ADMIXTURE was run for K=1–15. We extract marginal likelihoods from the log files to determine the optimal K, then plot ancestry barplots faceted by collection site for K=2 through the optimal K.

```{r}
# Parse marginal likelihoods from ADMIXTURE log files
struct_path <- "../results/admixture/"
fam <- read.table(file.path(struct_path, "Mytilus_structure.fam"), header=FALSE)
sample_ids <- fam$V2

log_files <- list.files(struct_path, pattern = "\\.log$", full.names=TRUE)
ml_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(log_files, function(f) {
  lines <- readLines(f)
  ml_lines <- grep("Marginal likelihood", lines, value=TRUE)
  ml_vals <- as.numeric(sub(".*= ", "", ml_lines))
  k <- as.numeric(sub(".*_K(\\d+)\\..*", "\\1", basename(f)))
  data.frame(K = k, best_ml = max(ml_vals))
}))
ml_df <- ml_df[order(ml_df$K),]
optimal_k <- ml_df$K[which.max(ml_df$best_ml)]

# Plot marginal likelihoods
p_choosek <- ggplot(ml_df, aes(x=K, y=best_ml)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept=optimal_k, linetype="dashed", color="red") +
  annotate("text", x=optimal_k+0.5, y=max(ml_df$best_ml), 
           label=paste("Optimal K =", optimal_k), hjust=0, color="red") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title="ADMIXTURE Model Selection", x="K", y="Marginal Likelihood")
p_choosek
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "ChooseK_plot.png"), p_choosek, width=8, height=5, dpi=300)

# Plot ancestry barplots for K=2 through optimal K (or K=4, whichever is larger)
k_range <- 2:max(optimal_k, 4)
ancestry_plots <- list()

for (k in k_range) {
  pattern <- paste0("\\.", k, "\\.meanQ$")
  qfile <- list.files(struct_path, pattern=pattern, full.names=TRUE)
  if (length(qfile) == 0) next
  
  slist <- readQ(files=qfile)
  rownames(slist[[1]]) <- sample_ids
  q_df <- as.data.frame(slist[[1]])
  q_df$Sample <- rownames(q_df)
  q_df <- left_join(q_df, metadata, by="Sample")
  
  q_long <- melt(q_df, id.vars=c("Sample", "Location", "Genotype"),
                 variable.name="Cluster", value.name="Proportion")
  
  p <- ggplot(q_long, aes(x=Sample, y=Proportion, fill=Cluster)) +
    geom_bar(stat="identity", width=1) +
    facet_grid(~Location, scales="free_x", space="free") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title=paste0("K = ", k), y="Ancestry Proportion", x="") +
    theme(axis.text.x=element_blank(), axis.ticks.x=element_blank(),
          strip.text=element_text(size=8), legend.position="none")
  
  ancestry_plots[[paste0("K", k)]] <- p
}

p_multi_k <- plot_grid(plotlist=ancestry_plots, ncol=1, align="v")
p_multi_k
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Ancestry_multiK.png"), p_multi_k, 
       width=12, height=3*length(ancestry_plots), dpi=300)
```

## 7. Pairwise Fst Heatmap
Fst values from the Stacks `populations` module quantify genetic differentiation between groups (G, T, F1, O). Higher Fst between G and T confirms species-level divergence.

```{r}
# Read the Fst summary matrix
fst_raw <- readLines(fst_spec_path)
# Parse the tab-delimited upper triangle matrix
pop_names <- strsplit(trimws(fst_raw[1]), "\\s+")[[1]]
n_pops <- length(pop_names)
fst_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow=n_pops, ncol=n_pops, dimnames=list(pop_names, pop_names))

for (i in 2:length(fst_raw)) {
  vals <- strsplit(trimws(fst_raw[i]), "\\s+")[[1]]
  row_name <- vals[1]
  fst_vals <- as.numeric(vals[-1])
  # Fill the upper triangle starting from column (i)
  if (length(fst_vals) > 0) {
    col_start <- i  # column index offset
    for (j in seq_along(fst_vals)) {
      fst_mat[row_name, pop_names[col_start - 1 + j]] <- fst_vals[j]
      fst_mat[pop_names[col_start - 1 + j], row_name] <- fst_vals[j]
    }
  }
}
diag(fst_mat) <- 0

# Convert to long format for ggplot
fst_long <- reshape2::melt(fst_mat, varnames=c("Pop1", "Pop2"), value.name="Fst")

p_fst <- ggplot(fst_long, aes(x=Pop1, y=Pop2, fill=Fst)) +
  geom_tile(color="white") +
  geom_text(aes(label=ifelse(is.na(Fst), "", round(Fst, 4))), size=4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="#2166ac", mid="#f7f7f7", high="#b2182b", 
                       midpoint=median(fst_long$Fst, na.rm=TRUE), na.value="grey90") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title="Pairwise Fst Between Genotype Groups", x="", y="") +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
p_fst
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Fst_heatmap.png"), p_fst, width=6, height=5, dpi=300)
write.csv(as.data.frame(fst_mat), file.path(out_dir, "Fst_matrix.csv"))
```

## 8. Diagnostic Allele Table per Individual
Using `triangulaR::specFreqDiff()`, we identify SNPs with allele frequency differences between G and T, then score each individual at those loci. This shows exactly which species' alleles each individual carries.

```{r}
# Get allele frequency differences at species-diagnostic loci
diag_freqs <- specFreqDiff(vcfR=vcf_hybrid, pm=hybrid_popmap, p1="G", p2="T", difference=0.8)

# Extract genotypes at diagnostic loci for ALL samples (full VCF)
diag_loci <- rownames(diag_freqs)
all_loci <- rownames(extract.gt(vcf_data))
diag_indices <- which(all_loci %in% diag_loci)

vcf_diag <- vcf_data[diag_indices]
gt_diag <- extract.gt(vcf_diag)

# Recode to allele dosage (0=homRef, 1=het, 2=homAlt)
gt_numeric <- gt_diag
gt_numeric[gt_numeric=="0/0" | gt_numeric=="0|0"] <- 0
gt_numeric[gt_numeric=="0/1" | gt_numeric=="1/0" | gt_numeric=="0|1" | gt_numeric=="1|0"] <- 1
gt_numeric[gt_numeric=="1/1" | gt_numeric=="1|1"] <- 2
gt_numeric[is.na(gt_diag)] <- NA
gt_numeric <- apply(gt_numeric, 2, as.numeric)
# Use actual loci names from the extracted genotypes (may differ in count from diag_loci
# if some loci weren't found or there are duplicates)
matched_loci <- rownames(gt_diag)
rownames(gt_numeric) <- matched_loci

# Determine which allele is G vs T at each locus
# Match diag_freqs rows to the loci actually present in gt_numeric
diag_freqs_matched <- diag_freqs[matched_loci, ]
# If p1 (G) freq > p2 (T) freq, REF=G allele → dosage 0=pure G, 2=pure T
# If p1 (G) freq < p2 (T) freq, ALT=G allele → dosage 0=pure T, 2=pure G
g_is_ref <- diag_freqs_matched$p1 > diag_freqs_matched$p2

# Calculate per-individual G-allele proportion across diagnostic loci
g_allele_prop <- sapply(colnames(gt_numeric), function(ind) {
  gts <- gt_numeric[, ind]
  # For loci where G=REF: G alleles = 2 - dosage; for G=ALT: G alleles = dosage
  g_alleles <- ifelse(g_is_ref, 2 - gts, gts)
  mean(g_alleles, na.rm=TRUE) / 2  # proportion of G alleles (0-1)
})

allele_summary <- data.frame(
  Sample = names(g_allele_prop),
  G_allele_prop = round(g_allele_prop, 4),
  T_allele_prop = round(1 - g_allele_prop, 4),
  N_diagnostic_loci = colSums(!is.na(gt_numeric))
) %>% left_join(metadata, by="Sample") %>%
  arrange(Location, G_allele_prop)

# Classify based on SNP ancestry
allele_summary <- allele_summary %>%
  mutate(SNP_class = case_when(
    G_allele_prop >= 0.9 ~ "Pure G",
    G_allele_prop <= 0.1 ~ "Pure T",
    G_allele_prop >= 0.4 & G_allele_prop <= 0.6 ~ "F1-like",
    TRUE ~ "Backcross/Introgressed"
  ))

knitr::kable(allele_summary, caption="Per-Individual Diagnostic Allele Summary")
write.csv(allele_summary, file.path(out_dir, "Diagnostic_allele_table.csv"), row.names=FALSE)

# Plot G-allele proportion by site
p_alleles <- ggplot(allele_summary, aes(x=reorder(Sample, G_allele_prop), 
                                         y=G_allele_prop, fill=Genotype)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  facet_grid(~Location, scales="free_x", space="free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("G"="#377eb8", "T"="#e41a1c", "F1"="#4daf4a", "O"="#984ea3")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), linetype="dashed", alpha=0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title="Proportion of M. galloprovincialis Alleles at Diagnostic SNPs",
       subtitle="Dashed lines: 0.1 (pure T), 0.5 (F1), 0.9 (pure G)",
       x="Individual", y="Proportion G Alleles") +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, size=6))
p_alleles
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Diagnostic_allele_barplot.png"), p_alleles, width=14, height=6, dpi=300)
```
